findings.resolution: Fixed in working tree; reuses upstream LRUCachePolicy and ChunkStatus with transactional byte-arena eviction candidate selection. Regression failed before fix and passes afterward.
findings.title: Custom byte arena misses upstream running-request prefix retention fix
findings.problem: Each prepare_store or prepare_load touches only the current batch. Eviction iterates OrderedDict insertion/last-touch order. Full request prefix order is restored only by on_request_finished. A running request stored over successive batches therefore makes its earliest prefix pages older than its tail, precisely the bug fixed upstream in e113018f5067045ac92de3949b8c302439abb226 (#61050). This file is unchanged from the old downstream tip.
findings.concrete_trigger: Use an arena of 192 bytes and 64-byte pages. Give request A keys p1,p2,p3 positions128,256,384. prepare_store/complete_store each key in separate batches without finalizing A. entries is now [p1,p2,p3]. A fourth single-page store, from A or another request, selects p1 as the first unpinned eviction victim. Prefix matching then loses all reusable history despite p2/p3 remaining resident. Upstream provisional request rank plus negative token position selects p3 instead.
findings.impact: Lower RAM-prefix hit rate and worse repeated-prompt TTFT under arena pressure, relevant to the deployed IndependentCPUOffloadingSpec and 8GiB arena. This is a missed upstream fix rather than a newly introduced memory-safety regression.
findings.suggested_correction: Adapt upstream LRU request-rank/position semantics to variable-sized host pages, ideally reusing the policy semantics while retaining transactional allocation and transfer pinning. Avoid rescanning and reordering the full prefix after every small store; upstream explicitly tests incremental complexity. Retain generation reset, failed-offer atomicity, and preservation of newer shared accesses.
validation_requested: Port test_unfinished_lru_prefix_survives_pressure_across_store_batches to BytePoolOffloadingManager, covering unequal groups and reverse transfer completion.
Cover running-request reused prefix plus new tail, out-of-order backfill, failed store retry, reset, and an old request observing a newer shared page.
Check incremental position lookups stay linear in the number of newly observed keys.
findings.uncertainty: Source-level deterministic trace; no runtime reproducer was executed because the candidate is changing and parent owns testing. Magnitude on real prompts depends on memory pressure and sharing.

findings.resolution: Fixed in working tree; get_load_source returns CacheHitSource.HOST. Regression failed before fix and passes afterward.
findings.title: Custom host cache reports unspecified external tier instead of HOST
findings.problem: BytePoolOffloadingManager implements lookup but does not override the new get_load_source interface. The base implementation at vllm/v1/kv_offload/base.py:320 returns CacheHitSource.EXTERNAL_UNSPECIFIED, whereas upstream CPUOffloadingManager returns CacheHitSource.HOST. Successful RAM hits therefore do not receive the same host-tier provenance as the upstream CPU cache.
findings.impact: Incorrect cache-tier attribution in v0.33's cache-source statistics; no transfer correctness or direct throughput effect.
findings.suggested_correction: Import CacheHitSource and implement get_load_source(key, req_context) returning CacheHitSource.HOST, following CPUOffloadingManager.
validation_requested: Assert a successful BytePool hit reports CacheHitSource.HOST through get_load_source.
findings.uncertainty: Observed by direct inheritance/source inspection. No runtime metrics endpoint was queried.

nonblocking_followups.title: Same-step sync restore needs ordering review before enabling on Mamba align profiles
nonblocking_followups.detail: Mamba align preprocess_state runs the fused recurrent-state precopy before early pre_forward initiates same-step synchronous loads. A boundary-crossing sync RAM hit may therefore copy a not-yet-restored source state into its next state slot. The active host is dense and does not enable sync_load_budget_bytes, so this is outside the current execution path and matches the original audit's instruction to leave sync loads off pending coverage.
nonblocking_followups.suggested_next_step: Keep sync_load_budget_bytes at zero. Before supporting hybrid synchronous loads, prove the precopy source/destination behavior with a boundary-crossing RAM hit and move sync restoration before state migration if needed.
nonblocking_followups.uncertainty: No GPU or CPU model execution; request initialization may eliminate some trigger cases. This is recorded as an ordering hazard rather than a demonstrated active-host bug.

verified_by_source_inspection.result: Offloading canonical mapping and worker registration derive num_blocks per actual group. Scheduler fence tracking uses cumulative physical pool offsets for allocations, copy-on-write destinations, partial/aligned handoffs and normal stores. The new upstream all-group allocation tracking remains before the num_external_tokens == 0 return.

verified_by_source_inspection.area: V2 store fence and load ordering
verified_by_source_inspection.result: KVarN prepare_cache_update runs before request updates that zero or copy cache pages; metadata identity prevents duplicate handle_preemptions between that call and pre_forward. Early pre_forward precedes mutable KVarN attention metadata construction. Independent worker copies remain synchronous, so accepting expedited=False satisfies the new submit_load contract without weakening completion guarantees.

v0.33 post_forward transfer collection before drafting and finalize_step after drafting remain intact. Deferred stores are queued after draft work, retaining draft-cache freshness. DFlash's num_speculative_tokens == 0 context-only cache maintenance remains intact.

OffloadingConnector.bind_kv_cache_manager binds replay_boundaries with coordinator.scheduler_block_size and bool(coordinator.drop_eagle_group_ids), preserving the new distinction between all draft groups and draft groups requiring the EAGLE lookahead drop. DFlash/DSpark are not accidentally treated as dropped EAGLE groups.

Pending stores and active loads pin pages. Failed multi-page offers allocate against copied free ranges and do not mutate state. Duplicate load keys increment/decrement references once while preserving transfer order. CPU sink restore clones payload ownership before arena space can be reused; sink byte accounting agrees between group configuration and KVarN serialization.

q_resident masks query_pos >= max_model_len and physical block0. Block-table column loads are clamped, positions are clamped for the attention pass, and masked query slots use PAD_SLOT_ID. Existing context rejected/null-slot masking and upstream K=0 branch remain intact.

Compressed-tensors and other non-ModelOpt configurations retain the local rename-mapper application and Qwen3 packed projection mapping. ModelOpt skips that preliminary mapping and receives the new upstream map_draft_quant_config helper exactly once, preserving upstream runtime prefix/layer aliases. This checks port preservation, not complete support for arbitrary compressed-tensors exact per-layer targets.

implementation: Upstream LRUCachePolicy owns request ranks, position ordering, explicit touches, finalization, newer shared accesses, reset generation, and transfer-pinning eligibility.
Entries share upstream ChunkStatus for the reference count rather than maintaining a second count.

A small policy subclass lazily inspects a heap snapshot only if allocation needs eviction. The arena commits removals only after every requested page fits, preserving failure atomicity. This adapter depends on upstream LRU heap internals and allocates a temporary heap list under pressure; no duplicate rank algorithm was introduced.
Request access recording forwards only newly seen keys and does not rescan prefix positions on incremental stores.

relevant_output: Both completion-order variants evicted position0 keys for groups0/1 instead of position2 tail keys.
